title: Grounding-field stripping can crash when resolved parameters are missing
reasoning: sanitize_and_validate_resolved_tool_call calls _strip_grounding_only_fields before validating executor arguments. _strip_grounding_only_fields unconditionally calls resolved_call.parameters.pop for mouse_control and scroll_control, while the later model validation explicitly tolerates missing parameters via resolved_call.parameters or {}. A malformed resolved call with parameters=None will therefore raise AttributeError during sanitization instead of returning the intended validation error message.
recommendation: Normalize resolved_call.parameters to an empty dict before stripping, or make _strip_grounding_only_fields return early when parameters is not a mutable dict. Then let model validation produce the controlled preparation error.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for malformed resolved calls, and the current order means the validation error path is bypassed before Pydantic can report missing required fields.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for sanitize_and_validate_resolved_tool_call on a mouse_control ResolvedToolCall with parameters=None and enabled=True, asserting a validation error string is returned and no AttributeError is raised.
minimumFixScope: Harden _strip_grounding_only_fields against None/non-dict parameters and add one validation regression test.
